issues.detail: English prompt says 400 words but kwargs check 336. Korean follows kwargs (336단어 이상), so it is consistent but differs from the English wording.
prompt_to_repeat contains both keywords '엄마' and '어머니', so the repeat alone satisfies keywords:existence. Same in English.
prompt_to_repeat contains '<<이름>>', so the repeat alone satisfies detectable_format:title. Same in English ('<<name>>').
prompt_to_repeat contains '쉼표(,)', so a verbatim repeat fails no_comma under strict scoring. English is also unsatisfiable ('brackets, i.e.'). Dropping '(,)' and the comma would fix it.
prompt_to_repeat contains '<<제목>>', so the repeat alone satisfies detectable_format:title. Same in English ('<<title>>').
Source keyword 'rte' is meaningless. The English substring check also matched 'shorter' and 'quarter'. Korean '알티이' must be written as a nonsense token, which makes the item harder.
English 'at least one' became '1개의 구역을 강조' (reads as exactly 1). Checker is >=1. An answer with several highlights passes despite the Korean wording. Use '최소 1개'.
In an XML answer, the closing tags after the last period count as an extra sentence. An honest 3-sentence XML summary therefore scores 4 and fails 'less than 4'. Same splitter behavior in English.
'para' was read as '단락' (paragraph). In English the substring 'para' also matched separate, prepare and compare, so the Korean item is stricter. Prompt and kwargs still agree.
'run' became the syllable '뛰'. The common verb 달리다 escapes it (false pass), and 뛰어나다 or 뛰어들다 trigger it (false fail). The prompt names '글자', so the item is self-consistent.
prompt_to_repeat contains '쉼표(,)', so a verbatim repeat always fails no_comma under strict scoring. Introduced by the translation: the English prompt_to_repeat has no comma.
